CORAM: HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA
ORAL JUDGMENT Heard the arguments from both sides.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award passed in M.V.C. No.1274/2021 dated 01.07.2024 by the MACT, Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru (SCCH- 25).

sentences.text: 3. Injured claimant, who is aged 51 years has met with an accident on 21.12.2020 and filed a claim petition claiming compensation of 35,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstance and evidence on record, has awarded the compensation of Rs.11,29,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
NC: 2026:KHC:203 HC-KAR 4.

Aggrieved by the said order, the appellant has preferred an appeal contending that the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during laid up period' is granted only for one month, though the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
Further, it is submitted that the compensation granted under the head of 'loss of amenities' also is on the lesser side.
The doctor has estimated the 'future medical expenses' at Rs.90,000/-.

But, the Tribunal has granted only Rs.30,000/- and it is submitted that the future prospects were not added while granting compensation under the head of 'loss of future earning capacity due to disability'.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: In the present case, the claimant was doing agricultural work and was earning an amount of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But he has not filed any income proof.

As the accident was occurred on 21.12.2020, the Tribunal has rightly taken the notional income as NC: 2026:KHC:203 HC-KAR Rs.14,500/- per month as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
He was aged 50 years as per Ex.P7-Aadhar card and the multiplier is taken as '13'.

6. The appellant/claimant has sustained the following injuries as per Ex.P5:
 i) Fracture of left humerus.
ii) Pubic and left sacroiliac joint dislocation.
iii) Fracture of sacrum.
iv) Fracture of T12 & L1 vertebral.

v) Mild left haemothorax.
 vi) Laceration over occipital region.
Out of 6 injuries, 1 to 5 are grievous in nature and 6th one is simple in nature.
7. The appellant/claimant was hospitalized for 10 days.
The Doctor has assessed the disability of the whole body as 26%.
The Tribunal has rightly taken 26% of the disability.
However, the future prospects were not added.
So as the claimant was aged 50 years, 10% is to be added towards his future prospects.

Therefore, the 'loss of future earning capacity due to disability' is assessed as Rs.14,500 + 10% x 12 x 13 x 26% = Rs.6,46,932/-.
NC: 2026:KHC:203 HC-KAR 8.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and period of hospitalization, this Court finds that the claimant might not have attended any other work at least for a period of four months.

Therefore,
for four months, the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during laid up period' comes to Rs.58,000/- (Rs.14,500 x 4 months).
9. Further, the compensation granted under the head of 'pain and suffering' is kept intact.

The compensation granted by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities' and 'attendant,
conveyance, food and nourishment charges' is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- and Rs.40,000/- respectively.

Further, PW2-doctor stated that the claimant requires another surgery for removal of the implants and estimated the cost of surgery as Rs.90,000/- and the Tribunal has granted only Rs.30,000/-
NC: 2026:KHC:203 HC-KAR towards 'future medical expenses' which is on the lower side.

The same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
10.

Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation:

 1. Pain and suffering 80,000.00

7 . Future Medical Expenses 50,000.00  Total 12,81,249.00 11.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.11,29,000/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.12,81,249/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,52,249/- (Rs.12,81,249 - Rs.11,29,000).
NC: 2026:KHC:203 HC-KAR 12.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in M.V.C. No.1274/2021 dated 01.07.2024 by the MACT, Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru (SCCH- 25), is hereby modified holding that the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,52,249/- along with interest @ 6% p.a.
